description.value: Ross Lake Campground sits on a glacier-carved reservoir deep in the Skagit Valley wilderness, adjacent to North Cascades National Park, with 50 km of trails and river fishing; the lake only reaches full pool in July–August, and the 60 km loose-surface logging road from Hope is the price of admission.

raw_osm.name: Ross Lake Campground
raw_osm.operator: Sea to Sky Park Services Ltd.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The fetched website is BC Parks' Skagit Valley Park page, which confirms Ross Lake Campground as an active 88-site provincial park campground accessed by ~60 km of gravel road from Hope. The website explicitly states 'there are no commercial facilities in the Skagit Valley that provide food, lodging, gas or any other goods or services,' providing direct negative evidence for food, fuel, vending, and ice; OSM tags (power_supply=no, internet_access=no) corroborate no device charging. The 'Book camping' header and 'Reservation policies' section confirm reservations are accepted.
concerns: OSM community is tagged 'Unknown / Okanagan & Thompson' but the park is geographically in the Lower Mainland / Fraser Valley region near Hope — community classification may be incorrect.
OSM phone number (+1-604-986-9371) belongs to operator Sea to Sky Park Services Ltd.; the BC Parks website does not list this number, so phone confirmation is not possible from the website alone.
No civic address is recorded in OSM; only directional driving instructions are available from the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active BC Parks campground with 88 sites in a scenic wilderness park; the remote gravel-road access and no-resupply-in-valley situation makes a WWC listing valuable to touring cyclists planning multi-day routes near the US border.
enrichment_extras.notes: Nearest sani-station is in Hope, BC (per website). Ross Lake reservoir is at full pool only in July and August; at other times there may be no water on the Canadian side. Bears are very active in this park.

wow_evidence: glacier-carved reservoir deep in the Skagit Valley wilderness, adjacent to North Cascades National Park, with 50 km of trails
